title: Write normal canonical files safely under retries and concurrent edits
description:
As a collaborating user, I want failed writes and stale edits to preserve committed content so history cannot silently disappear.

Feature: Safe canonical writes
  Scenario: Store every cloud payload canonically
    Given small and large issue, history and content payloads
    When cloud writes commit
    Then their exact canonical bytes are stored in S3 under normal Kanbus relative file paths
    And DynamoDB contains only query metadata, pointers, revision and hashes
  Scenario: Competing edits
    Given two clients editing the same committed revision
    When both attempt to publish their changes
    Then exactly one conditional write to the canonical issue file is accepted
    And the other receives a conflict without overwriting the winner or its history
  Scenario: Failed content upload
    Given an existing committed issue and history
    When a required object upload fails
    Then the failure outcome identifies which canonical files committed
    And catalog entries do not point to nonexistent or unverified content
    And incomplete multi-file mutations can be detected and repaired
  Scenario: Failed conditional issue write
    Given an existing issue revision
    When an S3 ETag condition rejects an issue-file update
    Then the winning canonical issue file remains unchanged
    And the rejected mutation is not reported as successful
  Scenario: Failed catalog projection
    Given a successfully written canonical issue file
    When catalog projection fails
    Then the operation reports the committed-versus-projection outcome accurately
    And retry or repair converges to that committed revision without duplicating events
  Scenario: Retry the same mutation
    Given a mutation with a stable operation identity and a repairable multi-file outcome
    When the client retries after losing the response
    Then the result distinguishes completion from partial recovery without duplicating a mutation or history event
